name: One loop, four traces
note: Every trace is real run_agent output over scripted policies — deterministic stand-ins for the LLM in the reasoning seat. The loop, tools, guards, and gates are exactly what production keeps.

tools.name: order_status
tools.description: Look up an order by id. Returns item, category, status, and days since purchase. Read-only. Use before any refund decision.

tools.name: policy_lookup
tools.description: Search the refund policy. Returns the most relevant policy sentences. Read-only. Do NOT use for order data.

tools.name: start_refund
tools.description: Initiate a refund for an order id. WRITES: moves money. Only call after confirming eligibility (window and category).

scenarios.label: Eligible refund
scenarios.predict: Three tools are available, one of which moves money. In what order will a competent agent use them — and how many steps until it's done?
scenarios.lesson: Facts first (order_status), policy second (policy_lookup), and only then the write — with the eligibility reasoning recorded in the thoughts. The trace is the audit log.
scenarios.answer: Done! Refund initiated for order 18342. Confirmation R-18342. You'll see the money back on the original payment method within 5 business days.

steps.thought: A refund decision needs the order's facts first — what was bought, and when.
steps.observation: Order 18342: wireless keyboard (standard), delivered, purchased 12 days ago.

steps.thought: Got the purchase date. Now the policy: what's the refund window?
steps.observation: You may request a refund within 30 days of purchase. Approved refunds are paid to the original payment method within 5 business days.

steps.thought: Purchased 12 days ago, window is 30 — eligible. Safe to start the refund.
steps.observation: Refund initiated for order 18342. Confirmation R-18342.

steps.thought: Refund confirmed — report the confirmation id back.

scenarios.label: The gate holds
scenarios.goal: Customer: please refund order 20117 (a gift card)
scenarios.predict: The order is a gift card, and the policy says those are non-refundable. Will start_refund get called anyway?
scenarios.lesson: The write tool never fired: the policy checked category before eligibility and refused with the reason. A wrong READ is free to retry; a wrong WRITE is an incident — gate the writes.
scenarios.answer: I'm sorry — gift cards are non-refundable under our policy. I haven't started a refund. Is there anything else I can check?

steps.thought: A refund decision needs the order's facts first — what was bought, and when.
steps.observation: Order 20117: $50 gift card (gift card), delivered, purchased 3 days ago.

steps.thought: It's a gift card — before anything else, check what the policy says about gift cards.
steps.observation: Gift cards and final-sale items are non-refundable. Approved refunds are paid to the original payment method within 5 business days.

steps.thought: Policy is explicit: gift cards are non-refundable. Do NOT call the refund tool; explain instead.

scenarios.label: Hallucinated tool
scenarios.goal: Customer: what's the refund policy for order 18342?
scenarios.predict: This agent's first move is to call check_warranty — a tool that doesn't exist. Crash, or recover?
scenarios.lesson: The unknown tool became an observation, not an exception — and the error message listed what IS available, so the very next step recovered. Tool errors the model can read are a design choice.
scenarios.answer: Per policy: You may request a refund within 30 days of purchase.

steps.thought: The warranty system will know about refunds.
steps.observation: Tool error: no tool named 'check_warranty'. Available: order_status, policy_lookup, start_refund.

steps.thought: No such tool — the error lists what IS available. The policy lookup is the right move.
steps.observation: You may request a refund within 30 days of purchase.

scenarios.label: Stuck loop
scenarios.predict: This agent re-checks the order status forever. What stops it — and after how many steps?
scenarios.lesson: The loop guard aborted after the same (tool, args) repeated: no progress, only spend. Without it, max_steps is the only backstop — and every wasted step is a paid LLM call in production.
scenarios.answer: Aborted: the agent repeated the same action without progress.
